description:
FOUND + FIXED s473t1 (Opus, the 13-file early-stop triage).  PRE-EXISTING
since commit 6b8e524c ("caller.t: perl-tests/t/op/caller.pl stub for XS
hint_fetch/hint_exists").

CAUSE.  perl-tests/caller.t line 336 is `do './op/caller.pl' or die $@;`.
perl's t/op/caller.pl is 175 lines shared between t/op/caller.t and
ext/XS-APItest/t/op.t and carries 47 assertions.  The copy in this repo was:

    # Stub: XS hint_fetch/hint_exists not available in PCL
    sub hint_fetch  { undef }
    sub hint_exists { 0 }
    1;

The stub's premise is FALSE: perl-tests/caller.t defines hint_fetch and
hint_exists ITSELF, in plain perl, at lines 141-152, over `(caller $n)[10]`.
Nothing XS is involved.  And because the stub returns 1, the `or die $@` never
fired: the file just ran 47 fewer rows, reported PARTIAL 65/112, and
baselines/row-shortfall.tsv said UNEXPLAINED.

FIX.  Restored from perl 5.40.3's t/op/caller.pl (byte copy).

MEASURED (--jobs 1, this tree): caller.t PARTIAL 15+49/112 -> OK 26+85/112.
+11 passing rows, +36 failing.  The 36 have ONE cause: PCL's `caller EXPR` in
list context returns FOUR elements where perl returns eleven, and element 10
-- the compile-time `%^H` hints hash the whole shared file reads -- is absent.
That is docs/not-supported.md 'Lexical compile-time hints ($^H / %^H scoping)'
plus '`caller()` filename and line number [DEFERRED]'.  Probed:

    sub f { BEGIN { $^H{dooot} = 42 } print hint_fetch('dooot') }
    perl 5.40.3 -> 42 ;  PCL -> NOHASH (caller(0) returns n=4)

GUARD: Pl/t/tap-assert-01.t row 22 (21 -> 22) -- two conjuncts, perl's own
first line and >= 40 assertions in the file.  Inverse-verified.
subject: DONE s473t1: perl-tests/t/op/caller.pl was a 4-line PCL STUB where perl ships 175 lines and 47 assertions -- caller.t produced 65 of its 112 rows and the hole was invisible (a `do FILE` that returns 1 having run nothing looks like success)
